transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is that I just cannot keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's really getting in the way of my work. Just one saw starting up in the shop, or somebody walking past the office, or even a random thought about another job will pull me completely off what I’m doing. And then... I don't know, the whole day just gets away from me.
Did you have problems paying attention or staying focused like this when you were a child?

Yes, I did. Even way back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother the same thing. They'd say I was bright, but careless. I was constantly losing my homework or forgetting the instructions they had just given us. I'd just be staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So, yeah, it was definitely an issue back then, too.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless or unable to sit still?

Yeah, I do. If I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or if I'm stuck sitting through a long meeting, I just feel... wound up inside. Like I really need to get up and move around. Even though my wrist is healed now and I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish what I'm doing, it's just really hard to sit there.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet when you have to sit still?

No, I don't really do that. I might feel kind of antsy inside, like I said, but I'm not really one to be tapping my feet or messing with my hands or anything like that. I just feel the urge to get up, mostly.
Do you often blurt out answers before other people have finished asking the question?
No, I don't think so. I usually just wait for people to finish what they're saying. That's not really something I've ever noticed myself doing.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn?

No, not really. I don't have an issue with that. Like, if I'm at the hardware store or the grocery store and there's a line, I just... wait. It doesn't really bother me. I'm pretty patient when it comes to waiting my turn.
Do you often leave your seat when you’re supposed to stay seated?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, my job keeps me on my feet most of the day anyway, being a carpenter. But if I'm somewhere I'm supposed to be sitting down, like a meeting or a waiting room, I just stay in my chair. I don't get up and walk around unless I'm supposed to.
Do you often feel like you are driven by a motor?
No, I don't feel like that. I'm usually pretty tired at the end of the day, honestly, not full of energy. I don't feel like I'm constantly on the go or driven by a motor or anything.
Do you often interrupt or intrude on other people’s conversations or activities?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really one to cut people off. If folks are talking, I just let them finish. And, you know, on the job site, if someone's working on something, I don't just jump in and take over. I just kind of keep to myself. So no, I wouldn't say I do that.
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss important details when you're doing work or other tasks?

Yeah, actually, I do that a lot. It's... it's a real problem at work. I keep putting the wrong measurements or part numbers down on my estimates. Like, I'll write 36 instead of 63, or I'll just completely miss a line on a permit form. And I usually don't even catch it until it's too late—like after the lumber is already ordered, or somebody actually has to tear out and redo the work because my numbers were off.
Do these attention problems cause difficulties for you outside of work too, such as at home or in other parts of your life?

Yeah, it definitely causes problems at home, too. My husband has actually had to take over doing the bills and keeping track of all our reminders. I just keep misplacing important papers or completely missing what needs to be done around the house, so it was just easier for him to handle it. 

And honestly, it's taking a big toll at work, beyond just writing the wrong numbers down. Those mistakes and the delays they cause have actually cost me commissions. Because it causes so much rework on the jobs, the rest of the crew is a lot less willing to rely on me for scheduling or ordering materials now. So, yeah, it really impacts just about everything.
Before age 12, did you also have trouble with impulsivity, like doing things without thinking first?

No, I don't remember having any issues with that back then. I wasn't really the type to act out or jump into things without thinking. I was mostly just quiet and kind of in my own world. So, no, impulsivity wasn't a problem for me as a kid.
As a child, were you often described as fidgety or unable to stay still?
No, not really. I wasn't a fidgety kid. Like I said, I was more the quiet type, just sort of zoning out a lot. I didn't have trouble sitting still or anything like that.
Do you often have trouble staying seated when you’re supposed to remain seated?
No, I don't have any trouble staying seated. I can sit still just fine. I'm not restless or anything like that.
Do you often feel like you have to keep moving or that you can’t relax, even when you’re trying to rest?

Well, I guess... if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or if I'm stuck sitting through a long meeting, I do feel really wound up inside. It's like I just need to get up and move around. Even though my wrist is healed now and I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish what I'm doing, I still get that wound-up feeling where it's hard to just relax.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet when you have to sit still?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really notice myself tapping my feet or messing with my hands when I'm sitting. I just sit there. It's more that internal feeling I mentioned, not so much moving my hands or feet around.
Do you often act without thinking first?

No, not really. I don't think I do that. Being a carpenter, you kind of learn early on that you have to think before you do something, or you end up ruining good wood and making a costly mistake. So, no, I usually plan things out and think it through before I act.
